Subject: Senior Infra Engineer — take-home assignment (instructions + deadline)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time to speak with us — we enjoyed the conversation. As discussed, attached is the take-home assignment for the Senior Infrastructure Engineer role. A few quick notes: 

- Deadline: Submit your PDF and code repo link by 11:59pm PT on Wednesday, Jan 14 (6 days). If you need more time, reply and we can discuss a short extension.
- Deliverables: PDF write-up (design + tradeoffs), a runnable example repo (link in PDF), and a short README with run instructions.
- Grading: We'll evaluate on correctness, system design clarity, and execution. We use a shared rubric attached for internal reviewers.

Attachments: infra-takehome-v1.pdf (assignment), grading-rubric-v2.xlsx (internal)

Next steps on our side: I'm coordinating reviewers and will send a quick calendar poll to the interviewer pool to lock scoring slots next week.

Please reply to confirm you received the assignment. Good luck!

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Technical Recruiter
Redwood Inference

--
Vanessa Ortiz

Got it — thanks for sending. I confirm receipt of infra-takehome-v1.pdf. I'll aim for the Jan 14 deadline. Two quick clarifying questions: 

1) For the code repo, is a short toy implementation enough (parked behind a simple Dockerfile), or do you expect a full end-to-end deployable?
2) Should I include performance numbers (latency/cost estimates) for the design, or keep it high level?

Thanks — appreciate the guidance.

Vanessa — TL;DR: toy implementation + perf estimate encouraged but not mandatory.

Details:
- Code: a succinct runnable example (Dockerfile + README + minimal scripts) is sufficient. We're trying to evaluate design thinking and correctness over polished production infra. If the candidate provides a deployed demo, that's a plus but not required.
- Perf numbers: include estimated latency and cost assumptions at a high level (ballpark numbers and bottleneck analysis). Precise microbenchmarks are not required.

I'll sign up for a scoring block on Tue Jan 13 morning. Laura, Marissa — can you both take one slot? Priyom, if you can cover late afternoon that would balance the panel.

Marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick questions — sorry for the delay. Per our internal reviewers: a short runnable example (Dockerfile + minimal code) is fine and preferred so we can run the candidate's demo locally. Including high-level performance estimates is encouraged (ballpark latency and cost assumptions + where you'd optimize). No need for microbenchmarks.

We've locked the scoring panel: Marcus (lead), Laura, Marissa, and Priyom will each review. We've scheduled scoring slots and added the rubric to the shared drive. Links below.

- Scoring poll / calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=reviewers-poll-jan2026
- Drive (assignment + rubric): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/assignments/infra-takehome-v1

If you anticipate a later submission, let me know by EOD tomorrow (Jan 14) and we'll consider a short one-day extension. Otherwise, we look forward to your submission.

Best of luck,
